title: This Business Makes Vending Machines Look Dumb
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Guest runs a YouTube channel about the business that the host links to; guest name-drops his best supplier Ranch House Meats

idea.name: Independent-store snack distribution route (jerky, candy, novelty)
idea.one_liner: Sign regional/local jerky and novelty candy brands, then sell, merchandise and restock full sections in independent gas stations, hardware and grocery stores every two weeks with buy-back guarantees, carrying stock on the truck for same-visit drops
idea.customer: independent gas stations, grocery, hardware and liquor stores
idea.offer: managed snack sections with free brand racks and buy-back of unsold items
idea.revenue_model: 30-45% markup on wholesale; ~30% net margin solo

key_quotes.quote: But then I looked into it more and holy crap, this guy's doing 50 to 60 grand a month and he's only been doing this for about a year.
And he started this business with almost no money because your customers pay you in 10 days.
I would say for gas stations, an average order, especially in the summer, is like 500 to 900 a delivery.
So 40, call it 40 gross and 30 net.

claims.quote: So I'm close to 100 now. So I'm like 94 95 accounts.

claims.claim: Supplier terms net 14-30, customers net 10: positive cash conversion
claims.quote: The manufacturers I'm I'm set up usually two um net like 14 to net 30.

claims.claim: Started with a $2,500 minimum order that included free racks
claims.quote: Like the more you buy, the cheaper you get, but they had the option of $2,500 order.

claims.claim: 40% of independent stores said yes early on
claims.quote: but at the very beginning, four out of 10 would say yes.

claims.claim: Only one account lost in the first year
claims.quote: I lost one account and I think about it all the time because I mean I was so excited to I just got these accounts.

claims.claim: A full rural route could gross ~$800K/year
claims.quote: And that full route gross should do like my route's not full and that's why I haven't done it yet.

acquisition_channels.details: walk into independent stores with a one-page sell sheet and product in the vehicle; revisit every other week
call brands without local distribution; call non-competing distributors in other regions for insight
brand sends a salesman to help open accounts; regional chain accounts

ideas.delivery: solo, 10-12 stores/day over a 2.5-hour radius; temperature-controlled storage unit/warehouse with staff receiving pallets (~$1,400/month for 1,500 sq ft); $10-12/month invoice app
ideas.other_uk_rules: Food business registration with local authority; food labelling and allergen rules for distributed goods

idea.name: Buy a neglected pastry distribution route
idea.one_liner: Bought a failing middleman's pastry route for $15K cash after stores complained of stockouts, grew it to two routes and sold them for $85K and $100K

key_quotes.quote: People kept complaining about this pastry company. They're like, "They sell so much.
I sold him I sold it to another guy for 100,000 the other route.
So, you you put 185 grand in your pocket.

idea.name: Bottom-up brand sales for a startup beverage
idea.one_liner: Get a new drink into regional store accounts first, then use the sell-in to land distributors; grew a CBD magnesium drink to hundreds of accounts and 8 Colorado distributors

key_quotes.quote: The distributor is not going to care to sell your product.
I think in Colorado alone, I we had like eight different distributors I opened up.

idea.name: Grow a route into a brand's exclusive territory contract
idea.one_liner: Distributor who sold random products built a territory and won a Red Bull distribution contract

key_quotes.quote: Like I have a buddy, he got a contract with Red Bull.

idea.name: Distribute syrups to coffee shops / supplies to restaurants
idea.one_liner: Same route model applied to coffee syrups or straws and napkins for restaurants

key_quotes.quote: I mean you can sell I know distributors um that sell syrups to coffee shops.

idea.name: Travelling novelty goods route
idea.one_liner: Retired couple in a truck camper sells fishing hooks, teddy bears, Montana shirts, shot glasses and knives to rural stores, dropping a few thousand dollars every couple of months

key_quotes.quote: They go every other couple months to a store, drop off few thousand bucks, never to see them again.
